question_en:
The Industrial History Museum plans to select exhibition plates from the scanned 1905 "List of Singer Sewing Machines" held by the Smithsonian. Examine the continuous section of machine plates: starting from the first two-page scan containing a machine illustration to the last two-page scan containing a machine illustration. Only plates showing the sewing machine and its complete floor stand or treadle stand from a front or front-oblique view, with the stand legs visible, qualify for exhibition drafting. Plates showing side views, only the machine head or partial tabletop, wall-mounted components, part diagrams, or those where the stand legs are cropped out require re-imaging. Please answer:

Which two-page scans are included in this machine plate section? List them item by item by scan number. Which scan numbers should proceed to exhibition drafting? Which scan numbers require re-imaging?

The answer must provide a complete itemized table of "Scan Number—Decision" by scan number, followed by a Q&A section listing the scan numbers for exhibition drafting and those requiring re-imaging separately.

## Step 01 · parse_task / Define set, image unit, and delivery fields

Action: Read the prompt, separate "full scope," "visual conditions," "itemized table," and "summary"; first establish the complete member list, then perform filtering.

Evidence Observation (Archived Evidence Summary): The 1905 "List of Singer Sewing Machines" held in Smithsonian record50, spanning from the first two-page scan containing a machine illustration to the last two-page scan containing a machine illustration.

Unified Decision Rule: A two-page scan qualifies for exhibition drafting if at least one image shows the machine and its complete floor stand or treadle stand from a front or front-oblique view, with the stand legs visible. Images showing only side views, the machine head, partial tabletops, wall-mounted components, parts, or those where the legs are cropped out do not qualify.
